text:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: pool3/card12: ECC corrected errors rising (24h: 3 -> 29), page_retire_count increment +26, recent Xid 79 spikes. Escalation score: medium. @infra-oncall please triage.

maya: saw the alert, pulling recent metrics. can someone grep dmesg on host gpu-3-12?

alex: grabbing logs now. ssh gpu-3-12 -> dmesg shows repeated lines:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (79): GPU exception on GPC 0: ECC error detected
[ 12345.679012] NVRM: Xid (79): Faulted channel: 0x00000005
[ 12346.000123] nvidia: page retired: 0xfffffffffffff -> incremented
```

maya: nvidia-smi quick dump (filtered):
```
# nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,uuid,name,remapped_rows,retired_pages --format=csv,noheader
0, GPU-aaaa, A100-SXM4-80GB, 0, 1
1, GPU-bbbb, A100-SXM4-80GB, 12, 27  <-- pool3/card12
2, GPU-cccc, A100-SXM4-80GB, 0, 0
```

alex: driver is 535.104.05 on that host, kernels match others in pool. BIOS fw 2.5.1. Not seeing a recent change.

taylor: 27 retired pages in 24h is worrying, but these are corrected ECCs not uncorrectable so machine still up. Can we run nv-hostengine diag or nvidia-bug-report to gather more?

liam: recommended triage steps: 1) set scheduler to avoid GPU for new jobs (drain) 2) trigger nvml error counters snapshot 3) if Xid rate keeps growing, mark for replacement and contact vendor RMA.

maya: put card12 into maintenance drain:
```
rbacctl set-host-drain gpu-3-12 --reason "memory-error_growth" --until 2025-07-01T04:00:00Z
```

infra-oncall: acked and applied. routing now avoids pool3/card12. rebalanced pods to pool3/card14 and dedicated-burst.

alex: pulled nvml counters: corrected_ecc=1340, corrected_ecc_last_24h=1268, retired_pages_total=27. I exported logs to s3://redwood-ops/gpu-dials/gpu-3-12/1755009123/ for vendor.

maya: quick cost note — rebalancing to burst pool uses smaller GPUs; expect ~8% latency increase for affected jobs. keep product informed.

taylor: I ran vendor diag script (attached in s3) — they asked for full bugreport and nvlink checks. I've scheduled swap window Friday 03:00-04:00 UTC, pending approval.

liam: before swap, try one more step: run memtest for the card to ensure it's physical. if memtest passes but retire counters still growing, it's likely firmware/hardware intermittent; vendor will want RMA.

infra-oncall: noted action items: (1) keep drained, (2) collect full bugreport + memtest results, (3) notify vendor and open RMA if memtest fails or counters keep increasing. Will update thread when memtest completes. :white_check_mark:

monitoring-bot: UPDATE: metric alert throttled -> continuing watch. next alert threshold at 50 retired pages.

maya: thanks all — please drop final logs into ticket INFRA-7892 and ping oncall once RMA created.
